formal_hypotheses.statement: E is compact in Euclidean R^n.

P.explanation: The source's nonnegative integer dimension is encoded by arbitrary n:ℕ, with H001:0≤n retained, and E is an arbitrary subset of EuclideanSpace ℝ (Fin n); H002 and H003 are precisely nonemptiness and Euclidean compactness. The canonical identification with R^n sends a vector to its n real coordinates and preserves the L2 metric in both directions. In dimension n+1, yHoriz extracts the first n coordinates and yVert the last; yJoin concatenates them. Thus z∈yProd E iff z is the specified coordinate concatenation of some x∈E and t∈[0,1], in both directions, including the empty horizontal vector for n=0. The target uses the same native extended-valued Hausdorff dimension and addition by one on both sides. It therefore states the whole original equality under exactly its original parameter domain and three hypotheses, without using a maximum-product metric or assuming dimension finite. Coordinate reconstruction and the L2 distance identity are local checked proof obligations at their uses in T006, T008, T010 and T013.

complete_formal_target.statement: V_K is nonzero, and for every K-linear subspace W⊆V_K, if W is invariant under the induced x,y,h then W={0} or W=V_K. Equivalently V(K) is irreducible as an L(K)-module. This holds for every given prime p, field K of characteristic p, integer 0≤λ<p, and arbitrary admissible lattice M, including λ=0 and p=2, without assuming K algebraically closed.
complete_formal_target.type: Target K M x y h

formal_hypotheses.statement: p is a prime number and K has characteristic p.

V is the complex irreducible highest-weight sl₂(ℂ)-module of highest weight λ, of complex dimension λ+1. The Chevalley generators x,y,h of sl₂(ℂ) act on V and satisfy [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h. In its universal enveloping algebra and in the induced operators on V, the bracket is [a,b]=ab−ba; the same symbols denote the corresponding operators.
formal_hypotheses.type: Module.Finite ℂ V ∧ Module.finrank ℂ V = (lam + 1).toNat ∧ h * x - x * h = (2 : ℂ) • x ∧ h * y - y * h = (-2 : ℂ) • y ∧ x * y - y * x = h ∧ Highest lam x h ∧ Simple x y h

formal_hypotheses.statement: v∈V is nonzero, xv=0, and hv=λv.
formal_hypotheses.type: v ≠ 0 ∧ x v = 0 ∧ h v = (lam : ℂ) • v

formal_hypotheses.statement: M⊂V is an arbitrary admissible lattice: a free abelian subgroup admitting an integer basis which is also a complex basis of V, and stable under U_Z. No minimal-lattice assumption is imposed.

P.explanation: For arbitrary prime p, arbitrary field K with CharP K p, integer 0≤λ<p, the given finite-dimensional complex irreducible highest-weight module and vector, and any admissible lattice M, H001–H005 encode the original hypotheses. The three endomorphisms give the Chevalley action through the relations [h,x]=2x, [h,y]=−2y, [x,y]=h; their invariant complex subspaces are exactly the sl₂-submodules, so Highest plus Simple describes the stated irreducible highest-weight module. H005 asserts the original integer/complex basis condition and all divided-power stability, equivalently U_Z-stability. There is no minimal-lattice assumption. Tensor commutation m⊗c↦c⊗m identifies source M⊗ℤK with VK; its inverse swaps factors and it intertwines all extended lattice operators. Target existentially constructs their restrictions a, requiring Agrees on every m∈M, so each restriction is unique and is the original lattice action. Conversely the original induced action supplies such a. Simple explicitly says Nontrivial VK and universally quantifies every K-submodule W with the three invariance hypotheses and conclusion W=⊥ or W=⊤. This is equivalent to the whole stated target because the three abstract Chevalley generators span L(K), including at p=2. No distinct reduced weights, algebraic closure, or positive λ is assumed; λ=0 remains allowed. Restriction existence is already a derived N002 obligation, not a new premise.

complete_formal_target.statement: For every t>0, e(·,t) is Lebesgue integrable on ℝ^n. The energy E:(0,∞)→ℝ is differentiable and E'(t)=0 for every t>0; consequently E is constant on (0,∞). The energy is exactly ∫_{ℝ^n}(|u_t|²+|Du|²) dx with no factor 1/2. No assertion at time zero is made.
complete_formal_target.type:
(∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → Integrable (fun x => WaveMap.density u x t)) ∧
  (∀ t : ℝ, 0 < t → HasDerivAt (WaveMap.energy u) 0 t) ∧
  (∀ (s t : ℝ), 0 < s → 0 < t → WaveMap.energy u s = WaveMap.energy u t)

formal_hypotheses.statement: n≥1 and m≥1 are integer dimensions.
For every x∈ℝ^n and t>0 there exists a real scalar a such that u_tt(x,t)−Delta u(x,t)=a u(x,t). No regularity of any selected scalar is assumed.
formal_hypotheses.type: ∀ (x : WaveMap.Space n) (t : ℝ), 0 < t → ∃ a : ℝ, WaveMap.utt u x t - WaveMap.laplace u x t = a • u (x,t)

formal_hypotheses.statement: For every pair of real times 0<s<t<∞ there exists a compact set C_[s,t]⊂ℝ^n such that u(x,r)=q whenever x∉C_[s,t] and r∈[s,t].
formal_hypotheses.type: ∀ (s t : ℝ), 0 < s → s < t → ∃ C : Set (WaveMap.Space n), IsCompact C ∧ ∀ x : WaveMap.Space n, x ∉ C → ∀ r ∈ Icc s t, u (x,r) = q

P.explanation: The parameters n,m are natural dimensions with H001 enforcing n,m≥1. Space d is standard real Euclidean d-space, with Fin d enumerating precisely the d original coordinates. H002 is joint C∞ regularity on the positive-time open set: ∞ in ℕ∞ω denotes all finite derivative orders and does not demand analyticity. The ambient total u represents the source positive-time map by restriction; conversely extend any source map arbitrarily (e.g. zero) on nonpositive times. All hypotheses and positive-time derivatives depend only on the restriction, so neither direction imposes an extension or boundary regularity assumption. H003 fixes a unit q; H004 is the original sphere condition. H005 is pointwise existence of a real scalar for the same normal acceleration, with no smooth scalar selection. H006 is the same compact support of u−q, locally uniform on each 0<s<t interval. Under smoothness, Fréchet derivatives on coordinate unit vectors and ordinary time derivatives give precisely the source component derivatives and Laplacian. volume is normalized Euclidean Lebesgue measure, and density is exactly ‖ut‖²+Σj‖uxj‖². The conclusion asserts integrability for every positive time, HasDerivAt energy 0 at every positive time, and equality of the energies at all positive time pairs. HasDerivAt is equivalent to differentiability together with derivative zero; the converse uses uniqueness of derivatives. Germ locality at t>0 makes this equivalent to the source energy on (0,∞), independent of the exterior representative. Thus the entire target, including all six hypotheses, time and spatial quantifiers, normalization and domain, is preserved in both directions. There are no E roots in the supplied source map.
